newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up from low prior close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up from low prior close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended up 60 basis points at 18 percent on Friday from an low unrepresentative previous close, traders said, adding that the rate had nonetheless closed below session highs on a strong peso and low U.S. long bond yields.
"The market was very firm due to exchange rate stability," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso ended 4.2 centavos stronger at 7.9070/7.9100 per dollar.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 15/32 to yield 6.88 percent.

Traders noted there was little volume during the session as many in Mexico were on vacation. Mexican financial markets closed on Thursday, May 1, for Labor Day and will close again to observe the anniversary of the battle of Puebla on Monday, May 5.
"There was some dealing in the money market, but rates did not change for much of the day," another trader said.
Dealers said rates also fell from initial levels on demand for paper ahead of forecast cuts in primary interest rates.
Money market analysts forecast rates on bellwether 29-day Cetes could fall by up to 75 basis points from a current 19.40 percent at next Tuesday's central bank auction of government securities.
The central bank drained 1.055 billion pesos from the system through a combination of three direct Cetes sales and two repos. One of the repos was assigned at four days at a rate of 18.00 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed unchanged at 19.25 percent.
June contracts for Cetes futures traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange closed up 23 centavos at 78.20 pesos.
Liquidity of 1.725 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Tuesday, the first working day of next week, from prior central bank participation.
